summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis, and anxiety was admitted for generalized weakness, urinary frequency, and a nonproductive cough after starting a generic antibiotic. Initial evaluation revealed elevated WBC and lactate, but cultures were negative. She was treated with IV antibiotics initially, transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for a presumed UTI. Her proximal muscle weakness, mild ptosis, and elevated inflammatory markers raised concern for a cryptogenic myopathy, though myasthenia gravis was not confirmed. Thyroid function was suboptimal, prompting an increase in levothyroxine from 100 to 112 mcg daily. She remained stable, with improving labs and no respiratory compromise. Discharged home with plans for outpatient neuromuscular neurology evaluation, continuation of ciprofloxacin, and follow-up on thyroid function.
